Megan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise summary and attached two artifacts: our manifest CSV template and a short overview of the sampling algorithm. I'll follow up with a proposed schedule and options (push to your S3 vs. Harbor SFTP). High level:

- Sampling approach: stratified time-window sampling with deterministic hashing for reproducibility. We pick contiguous day-blocks plus uniformly sampled tail events to preserve both chronology and rare-event coverage. The sampling seed is recorded in the manifest so audits can re-run the sampling deterministically.

- Manifest + checksums: every exported bundle includes a manifest CSV with one line per file: filename, byte_size, SHA256(hex), event_count, time_range_start, time_range_end, export_seed, redwood_export_id. The bundle-level artifact includes a top-level SHA256 over concatenated file-level checksums plus a signed manifest (ECDSA P-256) using Redwood's transfer signing key; we attach the public cert.

- Transfer modes: we support three delivery modes: (A) push to customer-managed S3 (we assume a presigned PUT or cross-account role); (B) SFTP push to Harbor-managed host; (C) one-time secure courier (for physical media). For S3 cross-account, files are uploaded with SSE-KMS and object tags indicating redwood_export_id and export_tier. For SFTP, we encrypt each archive with AES-256-GCM and provide an accompanying detached signature.

- Packaging & format: NDJSON per file, gzip compressed (.ndjson.gz) by default; optional parquet export for analytic needs. Manifests are UTF-8 CSV. File naming: <redwood_export_id>_<part_number>.ndjson.gz.

- Timeline & SLA for 30-day slice (~50M events): export prep (indexing & sampling): 6-12 hours depending on concurrency; extraction + checksum generation: 4-10 hours; upload: depends on network egress — estimate 3-8 hours for cross-account S3 at our baseline throughput. Total typical turnaround: 24 hours for standard exports; 48 hours if we need to run additional integrity passes or encryption rotations. We can commit to a 48-hour delivery SLA in our SOW for the production contract tier.

I attached the manifest template and a 2-page algorithm overview. Karthik and Naomi are cc'd to add any infra/security details. Happy to sync live Monday if you'd prefer.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_evidence_manifest_template.csv (CSV), export_sampling_algorithm-overview.pdf (PDF)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 01:12:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Evidence extract: sampling methodology + chain-of-custody plan

Megan / Jordan —

Following Jordan's note, a few implementation specifics from the infra side:

- Deterministic hashing: we use a keyed BLAKE2b-256 with an export_seed to select events. That protects reproducibility while preventing trivial cross-tenant correlation. The export_seed is logged in our tamper-evident export ledger.

- Hashing & signatures: file-level SHA256, bundle-level BLAKE2b, manifest signed with ECDSA-P256. We can provide the public key in PEM and optional PGP-encrypted signing if Harbor requires it.

- Integrity verification sample: as part of the handoff we will provide a verification script (python) that computes file hashes and validates the manifest and signature against the public cert. If you want, we can run an independent verification job against your S3 bucket post-upload and provide a verification report (timestamped and signed).

- Retention handling: exports created for audit are immutable within the export bucket for 90 days by default (object lock governance mode); after 90 days we can purge based on retention policy unless Harbor requests longer preservation windows. Permanent handoffs (customer-managed retention) are supported via cross-account copy.

I'll include a sample verification report in the follow-up.

—Karthik
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
